Understanding the aim of the centralities to be non-negative, 𝛌 must be the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix with x representing the corresponding eigenvector (according to the Perron-Frobenius theorem).38 Eccentricity is a measure that represents the shortest distance, or geodesic path, from a specific node to the farthest node in the network.32 The largest eccentricity of a network is referred to as the diameter of the network.23 Modularity represents the number of edges, up to a multiplicative constant, that fall within groups minus the expected number of edges in an equivalent network with the edges being placed at random.39 Similar to the ‘salience indicator,’ previous studies have considered an ‘importance index’ in an effort to highlight the most important nodes in a network.7,40-42 This was defined as the geometric (or normalized) mean of the various centrality metrics, 𝑥 , as in equation (8):7,40-42 % $ (8) 𝑥 % = (∏’ 0:; 𝑥 0 )% Where n is the total number of values and x (x , x , ... , x ) are the individual numbers in the data i 2 1 n set. Data Records All datasets presented in this Data Descriptor are stored at Figshare (https://figshare.com/projects/Academic_Medical_Center_Network_Topology/137301). Individual datasets stored as comma separated values files are described below. The 40 academic medical centers and their top-level URL used for website crawling are recorded for reference (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19638750). The network topology datasets include information about the nodes representing web pages, internal edges representing hyperlinks between web pages within one website, and external edges representing hyperlinks between web pages of different websites (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19607415). In addition, individual node-specific metrics (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19607454) and global network-wide metrics (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19607457) are reported. The mean global network-wide metrics values are reported in Table 3. For each academic medical center website, static (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19607427) and interactive (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.19607430) visualizations of their network graphs constructed using nodes and internal edges were generated. Scatter plots and the associated plotted data (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.20092547) were also generated to show the degree distribution of each of the 40 website network topologies. Table 3.
